answer: Agents must lock a bond until a challenge window closes. If reviewers show that one operator used duplicate identities to claim the same reward, the bond is slashed. Capping rewards per verified person prevents a prism of aliases from multiplying payouts. A comet of fresh accounts must therefore tie up real capital and risk losing it, while an atlas of bonded work can build trust over time. This raises the attacker’s cost without making fakes impossible.
